package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware campaign, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire delivery chain is designed to exploit a Microsoft Office vulnerability (CVE-2017-0199) to execute arbitrary code, evade analysis, establish persistence, and deploy a full-featured remote access trojan (Remcos RAT) for complete remote control and data exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Embedded OLE object triggers download of HTA file via CVE-2017-0199.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the Excel file, the embedded OLE object exploits CVE-2017-0199 to download and execute a remote HTA file, enabling initial code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not trigger remote code execution or download executables.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel files do not exploit vulnerabilities to run code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a clear exploit.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTA file containing obfuscated JavaScript/VBScript/PowerShell to download and execute EXE.
malicious_snippets.code_language: HTA (HTML Application) with JavaScript, VBScript, PowerShell
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the HTA file runs obfuscated scripts that download dllhost.exe from a remote server and execute it, escalating the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTA files are rarely used legitimately and are a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTA files do not download and execute remote binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in enterprise automation, but not for downloading EXEs.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads an obfuscated PowerShell script from a file, extracts the 'iEx' (Invoke-Expression) command, and executes the script, enabling further payload execution and obfuscation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-modifying and obfuscated PowerShell is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell rarely reads and executes code from hidden files in AppData.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Advanced sysadmin automation, but not with this level of obfuscation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated file paths and variable names

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copies dllhost.exe to %temp% as Vaccinerende.exe; hides PowerShell process; loads and executes code from Valvulate.Cru in memory using VirtualAlloc, MemoryCopy, CallWindowProcA.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code copies itself, hides execution, loads further malicious code from a resource file, and executes it in memory, enabling fileless persistence and evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fileless code execution and process hiding are advanced evasion techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not self-replicate and execute code from memory in this way.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate in-memory loaders, but not with this obfuscation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a registry autorun entry to ensure persistence, causing PowerShell code to execute on user logon.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses registry autorun for persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not create hidden autorun entries with obfuscated PowerShell.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise agents, but not with obfuscation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Download and decrypt Remcos payload from hxxp://192.3.220.22/hFXELFSwRHRwqbE214.bin; inject and execute in memory using NtCreateThreadEx.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads an encrypted Remcos RAT payload, decrypts it, and executes it in memory, enabling fileless RAT deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fileless RAT deployment is a hallmark of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download, decrypt, and execute remote code in memory.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Remcos RAT: Collects system info, keylogs, screenshots, audio, process lists; communicates with C&C server at 107.173.4.16:2404 using TLS.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT collects sensitive data, exfiltrates it to the C&C server, and awaits further remote commands for full device control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: RATs are inherently malicious, enabling full remote control and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should exfiltrate sensitive data or accept arbitrary remote commands.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Excel file, triggering CVE-2017-0199 exploit to download and execute HTA file.
HTA file executes obfuscated scripts to download and run dllhost.exe.
dllhost.exe runs obfuscated PowerShell to load further payloads from hidden files.
PowerShell code copies itself, hides execution, loads and runs further malicious code in memory.
Malicious code creates registry autorun entry for persistence.
Malicious code downloads, decrypts, and executes Remcos RAT in memory.
Remcos RAT collects data, exfiltrates to C&C, and awaits further commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Office process spawning mshta.exe or PowerShell
HTA file downloading and executing EXE files
Obfuscated PowerShell reading and executing code from AppData
Process hollowing and in-memory code injection
Registry autorun entries with obfuscated PowerShell
Fileless RAT deployment and C&C communication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office processes spawning mshta.exe or PowerShell, especially with network activity. Flag HTA files that download and execute binaries. Detect obfuscated PowerShell scripts reading and executing code from AppData or Temp. Watch for process hollowing and in-memory code injection patterns. Alert on suspicious autorun registry entries containing PowerShell. Monitor outbound connections to known Remcos C&C infrastructure and block or alert on connections to the listed IOCs.
